channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan family company to drill 10 wells for shale oil extraction
item.description: The Seytzhanov family's company, 'Souts-Oil', in partnership with Malaysia's ADIB Holdings, will drill 10 wells at the Karagansai field to extract shale oil. Modern hydraulic fracturing technologies are being used, with two horizontal wells already drilled. President Tokayev has previously instructed to create conditions for shale oil field development and attract investment.

item.title: Dushanbe hosts mining and metallurgy forum with over 200 international participants
item.description: The III International Mining and Metallurgy Forum of Tajikistan took place in Dushanbe on November 26, 2026, attracting over 200 foreign guests and around 20 Tajik mining companies. Organized by the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies, the event focused on investment opportunities and development prospects in the sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Creates Equal Conditions for Local and Foreign Businesses
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established equal conditions and support measures for both domestic and foreign businesses, according to Artem Novikov, Chairman of the Russian-Kyrgyz Development Fund. Speaking at an investment forum, Novikov noted a significant increase in investment activity and joint projects. The fund offers preferential financing and investment agreements for projects exceeding $10 million.

item.title: Foreign National Detained Attempting to Smuggle $200,000 Across Kazakhstan Border
item.description: A foreign national was apprehended at the Korday border crossing attempting to illegally transport $200,000. The Border Service of the National Security Committee reported that 59 attempts to smuggle undeclared cash, totaling over 508 million tenge, were detected between November 16-25. Authorities remind citizens that carrying more than $10,000 in cash out of Kazakhstan requires declaration.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Build 545 km of New Railway by 2030, Exempts Freight Wagon Imports from VAT
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement $8 billion worth of railway infrastructure projects by 2030, including 545 km of new lines, to increase freight capacity. The country will also exempt imports of freight wagons from VAT. The 'China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan' railway is expected to boost freight volume tenfold. International financial institutions and investors are invited to participate.

item.title: Woman Found Dead with Signs of Violent Death in Andijan Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: A 54-year-old woman was discovered deceased in a home in the Andijan region of Uzbekistan, with her hands and legs bound and showing signs of violent death. The Prosecutor General's Office has opened a criminal case for intentional homicide and robbery. Investigations are ongoing to identify the perpetrator.

item.title: Moscow Increases Patent Fees for Labor Migrants Starting January 1
item.description: Starting January 1, Moscow will raise patent fees for labor migrants. Under the new regulations, migrants working in private households will pay more for their patents. A minimum monthly income requirement to support themselves and their families has also been established.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Quality Road Construction Over Low Initial Costs
item.description: President Mirziyoyev emphasized the need for durable roads in Uzbekistan, stating a preference for quality construction over cheap initial costs that lead to future budget expenses. The country plans to implement polymer bitumen and geotextiles in road building, with production scaling up and mandatory application by 2027 for international roads.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tests Asphalt with Industrial Waste Additives, Showing Increased Strength
item.description: Kazakhstan is testing asphalt modified with industrial waste additives on an experimental 200-meter road section in the north. Initial tests indicate the modified asphalt is 50% stronger than conventional asphalt and shows a 35% reduction in water absorption. The durability against harsh winter conditions will be assessed after the 2026-2027 winter season.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Needs to Prioritize Strategic Scientific Directions, Including Biotechnology and Digital Economy
item.description: Tokon Mamytov, a public and political figure, stated that Kyrgyzstan should prioritize strategic scientific directions such as biotechnology, the digital economy, energy, ecology, medicine, and engineering technologies. He also emphasized the importance of artificial intelligence, big data, and ensuring water, energy, and food security for the country's independence and economic stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Invests $6.5 Billion in Road Infrastructure with International Bank Support
item.description: Uzbekistan is undertaking road infrastructure projects totaling $6.5 billion, with support from international financial institutions. Upcoming projects include the reconstruction of major road sections across five regions, supported by the EBRD, World Bank, ADB, and AIIB. Private sector involvement is also being sought for road construction and management.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Claims Unequal Conditions for Students Preparing for ORT Exam
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has stated that preparation for the General Republican Test (ORT) creates unequal conditions for students, as paid tutoring and services are not accessible to all families. MP Alisher Kozuev argued that students from wealthier families have a greater chance of achieving high scores, while the majority are overlooked. He proposed integrating ORT preparation into the school curriculum.

item.title: Prosecutor's Office Halts Unjustified Road Repair Spending of 272 Million Tenge in Uralsk
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Uralsk has identified violations in the procurement of a 272 million tenge road repair project. The city's housing and communal services department signed a contract for a 1.2 km road repair. The contract was terminated, preventing the unjustified expenditure of budget funds. The head of the department received a reprimand.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes New Tax Declaration Forms Effective 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service has proposed new unified tax declaration forms and instructions for public discussion. The aim is to simplify reporting by dividing declarations into three forms: for individuals, businesses, and civil servants. These new forms are planned for introduction starting January 1, 2027, to reduce reporting burdens.

item.title: Five Key Directions for Business Development in Kyrgyzstan Outlined
item.description: Temir Sariev, Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, identified five key directions for business development and improving the investment climate in Kyrgyzstan. These include protecting private property, ensuring legal stability, providing necessary infrastructure, expanding access to long-term financing, and attracting foreign capital and technology.

item.title: Over 100,000 individuals trained for upcoming maslikhat elections in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan has conducted approximately 6,000 training events for election commission members and participants involved in the upcoming maslikhat elections. A total of 101,896 people participated in these training sessions, according to the Central Election Commission secretary.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's CEC validates signatures for presidential candidate Zhapikeev
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan has confirmed the validity of 31,140 signatures collected in support of presidential candidate Syimyk Zhapikeev. A certificate of results was issued to the candidate's authorized representative after verification.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Ban on Foreigners Using Surrogacy Services Amidst Concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering tightening regulations on surrogacy, including restricting foreign citizens from accessing reproductive services. Proposed legal amendments aim to prohibit Kyrgyz citizens from acting as surrogates for foreigners and donating eggs or sperm. The changes also limit who can use surrogacy services to married couples and single women with medical indications.

item.title: New Cardiovascular Surgery Center Nears Completion in Kyrgyzstan, Boosting Capacity
item.description: A new five-story building for the Southern Regional Scientific Center of Cardiovascular Surgery is nearing completion in Manas, Kyrgyzstan. This project is expected to tenfold the number of open-heart surgeries performed and meet the needs of over 4 million residents in southern Kyrgyzstan. Professor Kaldarkbek Abdrakmanov, a renowned cardiac surgeon, is a key figure behind this development.

item.title: Almaty Dismantles Dropper Network Using Kyrgyz Students for Crypto Laundering
item.description: Authorities in Almaty have uncovered a network of 'droppers' who used bank accounts of Kyrgyz citizens, primarily students, to launder billions through cryptocurrency transactions. The suspects provided travel, accommodation, and funds to these individuals in exchange for access to their bank accounts for illicit crypto trading and online casino operations.

item.title: Underground synthetic drug lab dismantled in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region
item.description: Authorities in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region have shut down an underground laboratory producing synthetic drugs. During the operation, law enforcement seized approximately four kilograms of illicit substances, including Alpha-PVP, spice, and mephedrone. This action is estimated to have prevented the distribution of nearly 12,700 doses. A criminal case has been initiated against the suspected organizer.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to expand cooperation in the energy sector
item.description: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov presented the country's energy priorities at the 4th Belt and Road Energy Ministerial Conference in Qingdao, China. The conference, organized by China's National Energy Administration, brought together energy officials from over 20 countries. Discussions focused on strengthening energy security, developing supply routes, and balancing the energy transition.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes personal security services for tourists and businesses
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to offer personal security services to investors, tourists, and entrepreneurs. Authorities also intend to enhance the technical capabilities of security units, including the use of drones for surveillance. Proposals to improve security services were presented to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The initiative aims to integrate existing platforms into a unified 'Digital Security' system.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Emphasizes Quality and Modern Technology in Road Construction
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stressed the need for quality and modern technologies in road construction, prioritizing durable roads over cheap, short-term solutions. Starting March, Uzbekistan will produce 50,000 tons of polymer bitumen annually, increasing to 100,000 tons by year-end. The use of polymer bitumen and geotextiles will become mandatory for international roads next year.

item.title: Tashkent Police Accused of Illegal Search and Harassment of Minors
item.description: The son of a Gazeta.uz employee and his friend were allegedly subjected to an illegal search and intimidation by traffic police officers in Tashkent. The officers, citing a "Safe and Healthy Homeland" event, reportedly violated several laws. The parents have filed a complaint with the Ministry of Internal Affairs, awaiting an investigation into the officers' conduct.

item.title: Ukraine Denies Intent to Transfer War to Libya, Cites Russian Military Targets
item.description: Ukraine has no intention of transferring Russia's war to Libya or other countries, stated Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba. He clarified that operations near Libya targeted only Russian military assets involved in the conflict. Ukraine expressed regret for unintended consequences and reaffirmed support for Libya's sovereignty.

item.title: Lukashenko Claims Ignorance of Russia's 2022 Ukraine Invasion Plan
item.description: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko stated he was unaware of Russia's plan to invade Ukraine in 2022. He mentioned that troops gathered for joint military exercises before the invasion inexplicably turned towards Kyiv. Lukashenko used a map to illustrate the invasion routes into Ukraine.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Fergana Region Aims to Double Incomes for a Quarter of Residents by 2027
item.description: Fergana Region in Uzbekistan plans to double the incomes of 1.1 million residents, approximately a quarter of its population, by 2027. The region aims to reduce unemployment to 3% and poverty to 2.7% this year. Income growth will be a key performance indicator for regional leaders.

item.title: Temporary Ban on Trucks Imposed on Bishkek-Osh Highway Due to Snow
item.description: A temporary ban on all types of trucks has been imposed on the Bishkek-Osh highway due to snowfall and slippery road conditions. The restriction, effective from November 27 at 11:15 AM at the Sosnovka post, aims to prevent accidents and traffic congestion. Drivers are urged to follow traffic rules.

item.title: Eurasia National University Opens AI-Mental Lab for Psychological Research
item.description: A new laboratory, KazAI-Mental Lab, has opened at L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University, focusing on artificial intelligence in psychodiagnostics and crisis psychology. It aims to improve mental health services and digital technologies, and is the first specialized lab of its kind in Central Asia. The project also seeks to reduce stress and depression among youth.

item.title: Kazakhstan Border Guards Seize 59 Attempts to Illegally Export Currency in Ten Days
item.description: Kazakhstan's Border Service has thwarted 59 attempts to illegally transport undeclared currency totaling over 508 million tenge in a ten-day period. The seizures occurred between November 16 and 25 at border crossing points. The KNB reminded citizens that exporting cash foreign currency exceeding $10,000 is prohibited.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Secure $20 Million Loan at 1.5% for Rural Development
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to attract a $20 million loan with a 1.5% annual interest rate to develop rural areas. The funds will be used to improve infrastructure, support local businesses, and enhance production. This additional financing from the World Bank's International Development Association will expand the project's reach to 61 rural communities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prosecutor General Warns Against Election Law Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office has warned citizens to adhere to election laws ahead of the upcoming maslikhat elections. Violators face administrative and criminal liability. The office has identified 13 instances of election law breaches, including campaigning during a prohibited period. Those found guilty have been held accountable.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Five Toll Roads Worth $5.6 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to construct five new toll roads totaling 593 km, with an estimated cost of $5.6 billion. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need for attracting significant investment and new technologies in the road sector. The government aims to increase private sector participation to attract up to $20 billion.

item.title: Japan Grants $128,700 for New School Construction in Tajikistan's Tajikabad District
item.description: A new school has been completed in the village of Vahdat, Tajikabad district, Tajikistan, funded by a $128,700 grant from Japan. Previously, children had to travel to neighboring villages for education. The project aims to improve access to education for local residents.

item.title: Cold Snap Approaching Kazakhstan with Snow and Rain Forecasted for Weekend
item.description: Unstable weather, including snow, rain, fog, and icy conditions, is expected across most of Kazakhstan from November 28-30. Temperatures will gradually drop, with nighttime lows reaching -5 to -18 degrees Celsius by November 30, and even colder in mountainous areas.

item.title: AI Assists Kazakhstani Doctors in Diagnosing Stroke and Cancer
item.description: Artificial intelligence is now aiding medical professionals in Kazakhstan with the diagnosis of critical conditions such as stroke and cancer. This technological integration aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in the healthcare sector.

item.title: Nanjing to Host China-Central Asia and China-Kazakhstan Cooperation Forums
item.description: Nanjing will host the 13th China-Central Asia Cooperation Forum and the 4th China-Kazakhstan Interregional Cooperation Forum from November 30 to December 2, 2026. The events, themed around mutual benefit and high-quality development, aim to accelerate the construction of Nanjing as a key hub for the Belt and Road Initiative.

item.title: Lawyer Claims Rights Violations for Detained Kyrgyz Activist Kenzhebaev
item.description: The lawyer for detained Kyrgyz entrepreneur and opposition activist Syrgak Kenzhebaev claims his client's rights are being violated. He states that no investigative actions have been taken for over a month, and appeals to the Prosecutor General's Office and Interior Ministry remain unanswered. Kenzhebaev denies the charges, calling the case fabricated.

item.title: Uralsk Cancels 272 Million Tenge Road Repair Contract Amidst Procurement Violations
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Uralsk has ordered the cancellation of a 272 million tenge contract for road repairs due to violations of budget legislation. The city's housing and utilities department had awarded the contract for 1.2 km of road, but an investigation revealed a lack of economic justification and mismatched planned work. The contract was terminated to prevent unjustified spending.
